analysis: The code snippet calls serverName.substring(0, index) within a conditional block that checks index != -1. serverName is obtained from new JID(jid).getDomain(), which returns a string. index is the result of serverName.indexOf('.'). If index != -1, then index is a non-negative integer representing the position of the first dot. The substring call uses beginIndex=0, endIndex=index. According to the API, IndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown if beginIndex is negative, endIndex is larger than length, or beginIndex > endIndex. Since beginIndex=0 is non-negative, index is within [0, length-1] because indexOf returns -1 only when dot is absent, and we have checked it is not -1. So endIndex = index < length. Also beginIndex (0) <= index (since index >=0). Therefore all conditions for the exception are avoided. No exceptions will be thrown from this substring call.
answer: The only declared exception is IndexOutOfBoundsException. Its throwing condition is fully avoided by the preceding index != -1 check and the nature of indexOf.
remark: The substring call is only executed when index != -1, meaning a dot exists in serverName. In that case, index is the position of the dot, which is between 0 and serverName.length()-1 inclusive. With beginIndex=0 and endIndex=index, all conditions for IndexOutOfBoundsException are avoided: beginIndex is non-negative, endIndex is within string length, and beginIndex <= endIndex.
